content:
Schedule your Vision Meetings and team meetings in Everyfield, which announces each meeting to your Core Group and sends reminders to invited guests. Use a public church calendar to publish events, and use registration tools to collect sign-ups. Keep the handoff to children's check-in visible when you compare software. A form submission and a recorded arrival are different steps in the documented tools below.

Start with the features you can demonstrate. Everyfield doesn't publish a public calendar or handle children's check-in, so those jobs need another tool. This guide uses Google Calendar, Planning Center, and Breeze documentation as examples, without ranking them or recommending a vendor.

---

## Separate public events from private records

Google Calendar can share a public calendar through a link, and people can subscribe to it. Google warns that a calendar displayed on a searchable website can appear in search results. Treat public event information as public wherever you display it.

Keep children's registration responses out of public calendar descriptions. Use a separate, restricted place for family records, applying the FTC's advice to limit personal information access to people who need it for their work.

<Callout type="warning">
A shareable calendar link is not a private registration system. Review the public calendar and the family records separately, using the visibility and access controls each tool actually provides.
</Callout>

---

## Decide who can edit and publish

In Google Calendar, viewing event details, changing events, and managing sharing are different permissions. Choose the access that matches each person's responsibilities. For work or school calendars, the administrator controls whether sharing is available.

If your church uses an approval process, ask the provider to demonstrate it. Planning Center Calendar offers event-level approvals. Pending events under that setting stay off Church Center, shared calendar feeds, and kiosks until approved.

Check each publication destination. Planning Center documents separate controls for Church Center visibility and calendar feeds. An event unpublished in Church Center can still appear in an iCal feed. Use that distinction as a question when evaluating another platform, rather than assuming its controls work the same way.

---

## Compare the jobs you need done

Use this worksheet for a demonstration with your Technology Leader and Children's Ministry Leader. The examples identify documented capabilities, not promises that every product includes them.

| Job | What to ask the provider to show |
|---|---|
| Team meetings | Nothing: schedule these in Everyfield |
| Public calendar | How guests see events and how editors control sharing |
| Sign-up | How a form response reaches the family or attendee record |
| Arrival | How the team records a child as checked in |
| Pickup | How workers use parent labels and record checkout |

Google Calendar documents calendar sharing. Breeze documents forms that link responses to profiles, plus check-in and checkout settings. Planning Center documents event sign-ups and Check-Ins as connected products. Ask to see your intended combination working together.

---

## Trace registration through arrival and pickup

In Breeze, an event can limit its check-in list to respondents to selected forms. Its settings also offer a parent copy of a child's name tag and a checkout record. Being on the eligible list is distinct from recording check-in.

Planning Center supports sign-ups through Registrations and arrival through Check-Ins stations. Its Church Center app can generate a pre-check QR code. With Allow Complete Check-In turned off, the person must scan that code at a station to complete check-in.

<Callout type="tip">
Ask the provider to demonstrate the exact arrival setting you intend to use. Planning Center also offers a complete-check-in option without scanning when labels are removed. Do not assume that every app confirmation means someone has arrived at your station.
</Callout>

---

## Understand the federal privacy distinction

COPPA addresses covered operators of child-directed websites or online services for children under 13, and other operators with actual knowledge that they collect personal information online from children under 13.

The FTC says nonprofits generally are not subject to COPPA, while encouraging them to provide its protections to children. It also distinguishes information collected online from children from information adults provide about children.

Consider addressing your registration form to a parent or guardian. Have counsel and your provider review who actually supplies information and how the tool collects it, rather than treating the form's label as the whole review.

<Callout type="important">
Federal guidance and vendor features checked October 16, 2026. Confirm current COPPA guidance with the FTC and counsel, and current settings with your provider before launch. The nonprofit and adult-submission distinctions do not establish that every privacy obligation has been resolved.
</Callout>

---

## Collect less and restrict access

Use the FTC's business security guidance as a practical starting point for your church. It recommends collecting only necessary personal information and limiting access according to the work people do.

Review each proposed registration field with the Children's Ministry Leader. Ask what job it supports before adding it. A provider's ability to collect a field is not a reason to collect it.

Check the station screen as well as staff accounts. Breeze distinguishes a staff-facing list from its public kiosk mode, which it recommends when people should not see names outside their family. Ask your provider to demonstrate what a family can see at the station you plan to use.

---

## Rehearse with fictitious information

The FTC recommends fictitious information for training or development when real personal information is unnecessary. Use a test family to walk through the documented controls with your team.

- [ ] Open the public event and inspect its visibility.
- [ ] Submit a test registration and find the resulting profile or eligible attendee.
- [ ] Complete the configured arrival step and print the intended labels.
- [ ] Check the parent-label matching process and checkout record.
- [ ] Review what the public station displays about other families.

Compare the result with the provider's documentation. Bring questions about children's pickup procedures to the Children's Ministry Leader rather than trying to settle them through software settings alone.

---

## Plan access changes and retention

The FTC recommends procedures to remove access when workers leave or change responsibilities. Apply that advice when a staff member or volunteer hands off calendar or registration duties.

Write down what information you retain, why, how you secure it, and how you dispose of it. Check legal retention needs before choosing deletion rules. The FTC's records guidance ties retention to business or legal needs, rather than a universal period for every record.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"But all things must be done properly and in an orderly manner."* — 1 Corinthians 14:40 (LSB)
</Callout>
